newsitem.title: USA: Cobalt price to halve over next two years - Warburg.
newsitem.headline: Cobalt price to halve over next two years - Warburg.

text.p: Cobalt prices are forecast to tumble from an average $23 per pound this year to $16 in 1997 and $10 in 1998 as the market surplus grows, broker SBC Warburg said in its October International Mining Outlook.
Warburg said it was revising downwards its 1998 price forecast from $13 per pound previously.
Cobalt is a strategic metal used in magnets, aerospace alloys, and batteries.
The broker expected world market balance to shift to a surplus of 1,286 tonnes this year following a deficit of 670 tonnes in 1995.

Mine production this year is set to reach 25,600 tonnes, with a further 2,600 tonnes from secondary production and 1,242 tonnes from U.S. government stockpile sales. Demand is forecast at 28,156 tonnes.
Warburg expected the market surplus to rise to 2,692 tonnes in 1997, and to 5,672 tonnes in 1998.
"Beyond 1998 the outlook for cobalt is for the market to remain weak as a result of a number of major new mining projects expected to come on stream," Warburg said.
